done_when: Close writes the proof list from the tests it ran and their results, and the worker only names which Done-when item each test proves, so a proof list never names a test that did not run

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. `review.py:608` strips parameter IDs from both the worker's named pytest node and the reported node before comparing them. If the proof names `test_case[returning]` but Close runs only `test_case[new]`, Close publishes the unrun `returning` case as passed. The new command-level test uses only unparameterized cases, so it passes with this defect.
findings.title: Not done: Close writes the proof list from tests it ran, with their results, and names no test that did not run

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Test. At `test_close_checks_named_tests.py:37`, the test reads the `pr create` body file after Close finishes. The `body` helper (`tests/test_close.py:221`) opens that path then, and `_publish` rewrites the same file for the later update. The assertion can therefore pass even if `gh pr edit` never publishes the run results, leaving the pull request with its preliminary proof list. The test does not check that edit call.
findings.title: Not done: test_1_close_writes_the_proof_list_from_the_tests_it_ran

why: Workers write proof lists by hand, and about one review round in five is a gate on a missing or wrong test name in that list
